title: Protocol for live imaging of transferred mouse bone marrow cells by two-photon microscopy
protocol: Anesthetize the mouse with isoflurane vaporized at 4.0%–5.0% in an anesthesia box.
Place the anesthetized mouse on a paper towel.
Fasten an inhalation anesthesia tube to the nose of the mouse using cellophane tape for continuous anesthesia at 2.5%–3.5% isoflurane.
Shave the head hair with clippers.
Remove remaining hair with removal cream and a cotton swab.
Wipe off the hair removal cream completely from the shaved area.
Cut the skin in a cephalocaudal direction from the ear to the tip of the nose along the yellow dotted line.
Cut the skin in a proximodistal direction from the top of the head to the side of the ears along the yellow dotted line.
Remove excess skin by cutting along the yellow dotted line.
Apply hair removal cream to the skin using a cotton swab.
Wipe off the hair removal cream with a paper towel to completely remove the hair.
Pinch the skin with tweezers and split it longitudinally from the ear to the level of the nose tip using surgical scissors.
Cut the skin in a proximodistal direction from the top of the head to the side of the ears using surgical scissors.
Remove excess skin for later attachment of the plate to the bone.
Fix the head holder to the skull bone.
Flip the plate and adhere it to the skull bone.
Press the plate down gently.
Create a glue pool using “Aron Alpha” in the corner of the plate.
Fill in the gaps using the needle tip.
Apply Aron Alpha instant adhesive to a line 5 mm outside the window edge.
Apply tissue bond (M3) to the area inside of the Aron Alpha zone.
Flip the plate over and adhere the bonded side to the skull bone.
Press the plate down gently.
Allow the plate to stand for about 3 min until the adhesive dries.
Fill the gap between the head holder and the bone.
Create a glue pool using Aron Alpha in one corner of the right side of the hexagon of the head holder.
Stretch the adhesive along the hexagonal sides and fill in the gaps using the tip of a needle.
Perform the same technique on the left side.
Allow the plate to stand for about 15 min until the adhesive dries.
Pre-warm the stage to prevent thermal expansion.
Place the mouse on the stage.
Fill the gap between the skull bone surface and the head holder with PBS.
Securely tape the anesthesia tube in place after adjusting its position to fit the mouse's nose.
Tape the anesthesia tube to the stage before moving the mouse.
Fix the head holder and stage using two screws on each side.
Drip approximately 1 ml of PBS over the mortise of the head holder using a dropper.
Warm the tail on a 50 mL tube containing hot water.
Insert the needle into the caudal vein and check for back-flow of blood.
Glue the needle to the tail with Aron Alpha.
Tape the tube to the tail at an appropriate angle.
Fill a polypropylene conical tube (50 mL) with hot water.
Place the tail on the tube and warm it for a few minutes to dilate the tail vein.
Settle the injection line.
Fill the pre-made intravenous route with PBS using a syringe.
Insert the needle into the caudal vein.
Check for back-flow of blood from the tail vein to the needle.
Inject PBS and confirm that the needle tip is inserted in the vessel.
Glue the intravenous route to the mouse tail with Aron alpha A and Scotch tape.
Set up for imaging using a multi-photon microscope.
Start up the multi-photon microscope.
Turn on the heater in the environmental dark box for the laser and to stabilize the temperature.
Place the mouse fixed to the stage on the ThermoPlate inside an environmental dark box.
Connect the end of the anesthesia tube to the other end of the tube extending from the anesthetic machine to the environmental dark box.
Connect the anesthesia tube for the anesthetic machine to the mouse stage through the environmental dark box.
Connect the electrocardiographic monitoring system (optional) to the mouse stage through the environmental dark box.
Connect the syringe infusion pump to the mouse stage through the environmental dark box.
Intravenously inject 100 μL of blood vessel staining solution.
Inject the blood vessel staining solution continuously at a rate of 0.1 mL/h using the syringe infusion pump.
Look through the ocular lens using a mercury lamp and focus on the bone marrow cavity at an appropriate depth.
Determine the appropriate visual field to conduct time-lapse imaging.
Turn off all room lights.
Acquire imaging data.
Change the light source and light path to the femtosecond-pulsed infrared laser.
Set the excitation wavelength in the microscope software.
Set the zoom ratio in the microscope software.
Set the z-positions in the microscope software.
Set the interval time in the microscope software.
Set the duration time in the microscope software.
Commence imaging.
Monitor the heart rate of the mouse using an electrocardiographic monitoring system during time-lapse imaging.
Pre-process imaging data to remove background and accentuate the signal.
Use "background subtraction" method to remove the background.
Align drift using “Align” in NIS-Elements or "Correct drift" in Imaris.
Create images as tiff files from original file extension using software such as Fiji, NIS-Elements, or Imaris.
Create movies from tiff files using After Effects software.
Analyze images using Imaris software for cell dynamic analysis.
Measure cell movement, contact frequency, and duration of contact.
Design rendering automatically or semi-automatically using "Surface" mode for bone and blood vessels.
Use "Spot" mode for cells in the image.
Select appropriate algorithm at "Track Spots/Surface (over Time)" to track structures.
Create a channel representing the distance gradient of the surface by selecting "Distance transformation".
Choose "Outside of surface object" listed in the tool tab of Surface mode.
Measure distances from spots to surfaces using the created distance gradient channel.
